sections.html:
Brevard runs 72 miles along the central Florida east coast and has roughly 600,000 residents in 16 municipalities. Kennedy Space Center and Patrick Space Force Base are the two big demand drivers. A seller in Titusville, Melbourne, Palm Bay or a small beachside city deals with very different local governments, yet the tax bill runs on county rails wherever the house sits.

Permits depend on the address, while tax billing does not. On unincorporated land the county issues building permits, reviews plans and enforces code. Inside a city, the city does most of that. Before a pre-sale repair, confirm which jurisdiction issues the permit, since the mailing address on the tax bill can name a city different from the one that governs the lot.

The appraiser's office sets value, and the collector's office sends bills and takes the money. Nobody at the county's other offices sets your assessed value.

The collector publishes a calendar by month, and discounts run on the postmark. These are the entries a seller is most likely to need.

MonthWhat happens
NovemberCollection starts, 4% discount through November 30
December3% discount, third installment due December 31
January, February2% then 1% discount
MarchFull amount due March 31, fourth installment, last day for homestead tax deferral filing
AprilUnpaid taxes delinquent April 1, installment applications for next year accepted until May 1
MayDelinquent list advertised weekly for three weeks, cost added to the bill
JuneCertificate sale starts by June 1; first installment due June 30
SeptemberSecond installment due September 30

The plan is open when estimated tax is above $100. It splits the year into four payments, due by June 30, September 30, December 31 and March 31, and the application, Form DR-534, is due before May 1.

The June and September payments are figured from last year's gross tax. Changes from new value or exemptions are folded into the December and March payments once the roll is certified. After you enroll and stay current, you do not reapply each year, as long as the first payment arrives by June 30. If it has not arrived by July 31, participation is cancelled.

Anyone with a mortgage escrow account should skip installments, because the lender pays in November to capture the largest discount. Questions go to (321) 264-6969, and the form goes to the collector at P.O. Box 2500, Titusville, FL 32781-2500. Whatever is unpaid on April 1 follows the normal delinquency rules.

Standard bills are mailed by November 1, and the collector asks owners to call if nothing has arrived by the second week of November. Installment payers get bills quarterly, in June, September, December and March. A duplicate can be mailed on request.

  • E-checks made online are free, and a payment sent in error can be reversed by calling before 5:00 pm that day.
  • Credit and debit cards, Apple Pay and Google Pay carry a 2.75 percent fee with a $2.75 minimum. International cards are 3.95 percent. A third-party vendor keeps the fee.
  • A returned check draws a service charge under s. 68.065: $25 under $50, $30 from $50 to $299.99, $40 from $300 to $799.99, and 5 percent at $800 or more.
  • Wire payments must name the tax account number, the owner and the property ID, and cover all bank fees.

A current mailing address on file protects against ownership problems, which matters most for an owner who has already moved out.

In May the late list for real estate is printed in a local paper on three consecutive weeks, and the ad cost plus an electronic fee land on the owner's balance. Certificates go up for sale as early as June 1 or soon after. Late business property gets one May listing, and warrants follow July 1.

A holder who has waited out the statutory period may then apply for a deed under s. 197.502. On a homestead, the opening bid includes half of the last assessed value, and a homestead balance under $250 is issued to the county, never auctioned.

sections.h2: Can the sale close while tax is unpaid?
sections.html:
Yes. Back taxes will not block a closing. The title agent still needs the collector's payoff and any certificate costs, so request them early. A sold certificate has to be redeemed at the table.

A deed to the buyer also resets the parcel to just value on January 1, which ends the homestead growth limit, so the buyer's first bill can sit far above yours. If you are moving to another Florida house, ask about portability and Form DR-501T.

Start with the Brevard County Property Appraiser at (321) 264-6700. If the record misstates something simple, such as the bedroom count, a phone call may settle it. Formal petitions use the DR-486 forms and are filed with the clerk within 25 days of the August notice, or 30 days after an exemption denial letter.

Homestead applications are due March 1. Amendment 3, a homestead exemption ballot item, may change exemption amounts, so check the appraiser's site before you quote a buyer next year's taxes.

sections.h2: Relief programs for older or military-connected owners
sections.html:
Several programs depend on local adoption, so ask the appraiser which apply in Brevard and your city.

  • Residents 65 and older: an ordinance may add as much as $50,000 for qualifying household income.
  • Disabled ex-servicemembers: a $5,000 assessed value reduction.
  • Former servicemembers past 65 with a lasting service-related disability: a homestead discount tied to the VA percentage.
  • Homestead tax deferral: March 31 is the filing deadline.

Heirs lose the exemption once the owner is gone. Call the appraiser to learn how the transfer is treated, since certain transfers at death escape the ownership reset, and pull a payoff from the collector before the sign goes up.

Gather the deed or probate paperwork, the latest tax bill and the parcel number first. Ask the title agent to run a lien search so any certificate or unpaid balance is found while there is still time to deal with it.

Bring your deed, the most recent tax bill, the collector's written payoff and any letter confirming an exemption. If you used the installment plan, bring a record of the payments made so the title agent can show what is already paid. Keep a copy of the final settlement statement with your tax records, because questions about the closing figures can come back months later.

sections.h2: Before you list a Brevard house
sections.html:
A few calls early in the process save trouble later.

  1. Phone the collector for the current balance and ask whether any installment plan, deferral or certificate is attached to the parcel.
  2. Phone the appraiser to confirm the owner name, mailing address and any exemption in your name.
  3. Check which government issues permits for the lot before any repair.
  4. Give the written figures to your title agent so they appear on the closing statement.

A cash buyer can close without waiting on a lender, though the payoff, the proration and the deed still need the same care.

faqs.q: Which Brevard office mails the tax notice?
faqs.a: The tax collector mails the November bill. The property appraiser mails the proposed tax notice in August.

faqs.q: What is the Brevard delinquency date?
faqs.a: April 1. Taxes unpaid then become delinquent, and certificates are offered on or before June 1.

faqs.q: What is the minimum for the Brevard installment plan?
faqs.a: Estimated tax must exceed $100, and the application on Form DR-534 must reach the collector before May 1.

faqs.q: Do mortgage escrow owners use installments in Brevard?
faqs.a: No. Lenders pay in November to capture the discount, so installments are not for escrow accounts.

faqs.q: Is the Brevard discount based on postmark?
faqs.a: Yes. Discounts follow the postmark, with 4 percent through November 30.
